candidates.title: A CPU Inside an LLM: Zero-Gradient Compilation of Exact Circuits into Pretrained Weights
candidates.content: Pretrained language models (LMs) remain unreliable on exact multi-digit arithmetic without gradient fine-tuning or external tool interpreters. We introduce closed-form, zero-gradient circuit-grafting primitives that compile deterministic computation directly into pretrained LM weights using zero training examples and zero runtime hooks, while bounding per-layer normalization drift and preserving natural-language (NL) competence. Our construction combines three analytical mechanisms: (1) two-layer Mellin-GLU quadrature over bias-free SwiGLU/GeGLU layers, turning unknown per-token RMSNorm scaling into translation along a log-spaced gate grid (>250times dynamic range) with IEEE 754 error bounds; (2) cross-token scale cancellation via signed Chebyshev Indefinite-RoPE self-sink attention and memoryless SiLU-antisymmetric GatedDeltaNet shifts; and (3) axis-aligned width extension (d to d+K) with d/(d+K) norm compensation, Base-1000 canonical BPE emission, and differential (+254,-256) tied unembeddings. candidates.title: Phantom Success, Silent Failure: Auditing the Success Checkers of Simulated Manipulation Benchmarks
candidates.content: Simulated manipulation benchmarks measure policy performance using hand-written success checkers that label each episode as a success or failure. Passing an expert demonstration shows that a checker accepts one way of completing the task. Learned policies, however, may stop after partial progress or complete the task in a different way. A checker may then accept an incomplete execution (phantom success) or reject an execution that satisfies the instruction (silent failure). In this paper, we introduce SimAudit, an LLM-based pipeline that audits success checkers against task instructions. SimAudit analyzes the instruction and checker code to identify scenarios where the two may disagree, recreates those scenarios in simulation, and runs the original checker. Multi-view renderings are then used to verify whether the observed behavior satisfies the instruction. Across RoboTwin 2.0, RoboCasa365, and RoboDojo, 183 simulated test cases produced the predicted checker verdict. Visual verification and deduplication yielded 61 distinct defects across 49 tasks, including 40 phantom successes and 21 silent failures. candidates.title: PAD: Policy-Aware Data Valuation for Autonomous Driving
candidates.content: End-to-end autonomous driving increasingly depends on scaling training demonstrations, yet data growth does not guarantee proportional gains. However, additional data do not guarantee better policies: a demonstration that benefits one planner may be redundant or harmful to another. Existing curation methods typically infer data value from intrinsic sample properties or training-dependent proxies that do not measure downstream policy utility. To address this, we introduce Policy-Aware Data Valuation (PAD), a framework that assigns each candidate demonstration a utility specific to the target driving policy. PAD combines scene-level calibration feedback with projected policy gradients and a regularized approximation of local training geometry, producing scalable influence-based values for the policy. A controlled group-removal study establishes the directional fidelity of these values, while cross-planner analysis shows that the same candidate pool induces markedly different rankings across planner families. candidates.title: Safety and Immunogenicity of Innocell Autologous Cellular Immunotherapy for Recurrent Epithelial Ovarian Cancer
candidates.content: [PHASE1] RECRUITING | 申办方/赞助方: PhotonPharma, Inc. | 适应症: Ovarian Cancer (OvCa). This is a Phase 1 study to evaluate the safety and immunogenicity of Innocell, an autologous cellular immunotherapy made from patient-derived tumor cells, in female patients with recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer. Innocell autologous cellular immunotherapy consists of autologous tumor cells which have been inactivated using a proprietary light technology that inhibits cell replication while allowing for the cell to maintain antigen expression. These replication incompetent cells are then administered concurrently with an immunoadjuvant to stimulate a person's innate or adaptive immune response to vaccine antigens. This novel inactivation mechanism creates improved antigen presentation, specifically with presentation of the broad array of neoantigens unique to each patient's tumor.

candidates.title: Improving Vaccine Efficacy for People With Helminth Infection: CORBEVAX in Ethiopia
candidates.content: [PHASE2,PHASE3] RECRUITING | 申办方/赞助方: University of Aarhus | 适应症: Schistosomiasis Mansoni, Hookworm Infection, COVID-19. Helminth infections affect over 1.5 billion people and weaken the response to vaccination. CORBEVAX contains the TLR9-activating adjuvant CpG 1018, which may overcome this. This trial measures the immunogenicity of CORBEVAX in adults with and without Schistosoma mansoni or hookworm infection in Ethiopia. The primary measure is spike-specific serum IgG at Day 42; antibody subclass, T-cell, neutralisation and regulatory T-cell responses are measured as secondary outcomes up to Day 90. This is the first of two planned cohorts under a shared protocol; a second cohort receiving an mRNA COVID-19 vaccine at the same sites is planned subject to vaccine availability and will be registered separately.

candidates.title: A Study to Learn About Revaccination With a Vaccine Called RSVpreF in Immunocompromised Adults
candidates.content: [PHASE3] RECRUITING | 申办方/赞助方: Pfizer | 适应症: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV). The purpose of this phase 3 study is to learn the safety, tolerability and immunogenicity of revaccination with RSVpreF at approximately 1-, 2-, and 3-year intervals to inform the revaccination interval in immunocompromised adults. This study is seeking participants who are 18 years of age and older and will be grouped based on prior RSV vaccination history. Participants are required to be immunocompromised per study protocol. All participants in this study will receive 1 shot to their arm of a RSVPreF vaccine. Participants will take part in this study for about 12 months and will need to visit the clinical study site at least 4 times.

candidates.title: Xist deletion in T cells protects against influenza-induced lung injury
candidates.content: Sex differences in antiviral immunity are well established, yet the contribution of X-Chromosome Inactivation (XCI) to T cell responses during infection is unknown. Here, we identify an unexpected role for Xist RNA in shaping T cell immunity and pulmonary injury following influenza infection. We show that the inactive X chromosome (Xi) in pulmonary CD4+ and CD8+ T cells undergoes dynamic epigenetic remodeling, with limited Xist RNA localization, differential enrichment of H3K27me3 and H2AK119Ub modifications, and activation-dependent XCI escape of immune-related genes, including Il2rg and Cxcr3. Remarkably, T cell-specific Xist deletion protects female mice from influenza-induced weight loss and pulmonary pathology despite comparable early viral burdens. Transcriptomic profiling reveals increased expression of X-linked escape genes and antiviral and interferon-responsive genes, particularly in CD8+ T cells. Furthermore, Xist-deficient CD4+ and CD8+ antigen-experienced (CD44+CD11a+) T cells exhibit increased biallelic Cxcr3 expression, elevated pulmonary Cxcr3 protein levels, and enhanced IFN-{gamma} and TNF responses following ex vivo stimulation. candidates.title: Keratinocyte IL-17RA signaling promotes neutrophil recruitment and clinical lesions in experimental epidermolysis bullosa
candidates.content: Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita (EBA) is an autoimmune blistering disease (AIBD) characterized by anti-type VII collagen autoantibody-mediated tissue injury. Neutrophils have been identified as essential for dermal-epidermal separation in various in vitro and mouse models of EBA. Although interleukin-17 (IL-17) signaling promotes neutrophilic inflammation, its contribution to EBA and the relevant responding cell types remain poorly defined. We investigated the role and cellular targets of IL-17 receptor A (IL-17RA) signaling using an antibody-transfer model of EBA in mice with global IL-17RA deficiency, combined IL-17A/IL-17F deficiency, IL-17F deficiency, or myeloid cell- or keratinocyte-specific IL-17RA deletion. Complementary in vitro assays assessed IL-17A-induced chemokine expression and neutrophil migration. Global IL-17RA deficiency, combined IL-17A/IL-17F deficiency, and IL-17F deficiency significantly reduced disease severity in vivo. Keratinocyte-specific IL-17RA deletion markedly attenuated EBA, whereas myeloid cell-specific deletion did not confer protection. candidates.title: GRABS: a content-addressed antibody-antigen binding-affinity dataset with predicted structures and a leak-free benchmark
candidates.content: Machine-learning prediction of antibody-antigen binding affinity depends as much on the training data as on the model, yet public affinity measurements are scattered across databases with incompatible formats, mix genuine dissociation constants with censored or predicted values, and concentrate most of their label mass on a few heavily mutated targets. We present GRABS (Geometric Resource for Antibody Binding Studies), a curated, content-addressed, structure-ready dataset that consolidates nine public sources, of which the seven with redistributable licenses yield 4,380 canonical antibody-antigen records} (median-collapsed from 4,761 raw measurements), each with an experimentally measured dissociation constant (Kd), paired heavy and light variable regions (VH, VL), and an antigen sequence, covering 2,015 distinct antigen sequences. Every structure, graph, and feature is addressed by a content key, md5(VH+VL+antigen)[:10], and verified non-circularly: each graph's node features are decoded back to sequence and re-hashed, matching the content key for 4,282/4,282 (100%) structure-backed records.
